explanation: Chaplin held out against dialogue for years: City Lights (1931) and Modern Times (1936) use music and sound effects. His first true talkie was The Great Dictator (1940).

claims.text: The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson, was released in 1927.
Charlie Chaplin's first full talking film was The Great Dictator, released in 1940.
City Lights (1931) and Modern Times (1936) have synchronized music and sound effects but almost no spoken dialogue.
